title: The Effect of Periodization and Training Intensity Distribution on Middle- and Long-Distance Running Performance: A Systematic Review
authors: Kenneally M, Casado A, Santos-Concejero J
journal: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
population: Middle- and long-distance runners; 16 studies (6 observational, 3 case studies, 6 interventions, 1 review) of programs lasting 4 weeks or more
findings: Searched May 2017; 493 articles screened and 16 included.
Pyramidal and polarized training appear more effective than threshold training, although threshold training is used by some of the best marathon runners in the world.
Review proposes defining zones as a percentage of goal race pace so different periodization types can be reconciled; authors state this approach needs further development.
limitations: Heterogeneous and mostly non-randomized studies; race-pace zone percentages not validated; predates 2019-2025 meta-analyses.
implications: Define race-specific intensity relative to goal race pace as well as physiological anchors.
Do not prohibit threshold work: some elite marathoners succeed with substantial threshold volume; the evidence is against threshold-dominant defaults, not against threshold sessions.
